covers: how to graph the solution set of an inequality on a number line, with an open or closed circle at the boundary point and a ray in the right direction

intro.caption: Lesson 8-5 — graphing inequalities on a number line. Every ride at Screamline Park needs a sign that shows who can ride. Hana runs the sign shop. Three gates and a boss sign stand between the interns and an open park.

balloons.t: Every ride sign needs a number line. It shows ALL the riders who can go. No sign, no ride. Rules are rules.
Gus painted the first batch. With the mascot head ON. This should be good.
Go-karts: taller than 47 inches. I painted a filled-in dot on 47. Done!
Filled-in means 47 counts. But is 47 taller than 47?

pages.caption: Gus put a closed circle at 47. A closed circle says 47 is in the solution set. But 47 > 47 is not a true statement.

balloons.t: First the circle. Is the boundary point a solution, or not?
The Mini Drop is for little kids. Riders must be shorter than 54 inches.
My arrow points right. Right is the good side. Right?
Two signs left: the Screamer coaster and the Kiddie Cups. Circle first, then the arrow.
I am not in the solution set for teacups. I am in it for funnel cake.
I inspect every sign. One wrong circle and the ride stays closed. Rules are rules.
Bring it. My circles are perfect.
Every sign is right. Funnel cake ≥ 1 for me.

win.caption: A graph of an inequality shows every solution. Put a circle on the boundary point: closed (●) for ≤ or ≥, open (○) for < or >. Then draw the ray: right for greater, left for less.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Open or Closed?
gates.prompt: The Go-Kart rule is h > 47 inches. Decide if the boundary point is in the solution set.
hints: Conceptual: a closed circle means the boundary number IS a solution. An open circle means it is NOT. Only ≤ and ≥ include the boundary.
Procedural: put the boundary number into the inequality. If you get a true statement, fill the circle. If it is false, leave it open.

steps: Practice rule: t < 9. The boundary point is 9.
Test 9: is 9 < 9? No. That is false, so 9 is not a solution.
So the circle at 9 is open (○).
worked.q: Open or closed circle for x ≥ 15?

options.fb: That is Gus's mistake. > means greater than, not equal. 47 > 47 is false, so 47 is not included.

options.t: An open circle — 47 is not included
No circle — just paint the arrow
options.fb: Every graph needs a circle on the boundary point. It shows where the solution set starts.

items.label: Shortest whole-number height (inches) that can drive:
items.aria: shortest whole number height in inches that can drive a go-kart

fb.msg: Test it: 47 > 47 is false. The open circle means 47 is NOT in the solution set.
46 is shorter than 47. The rule needs riders taller than 47.

items.fbDefault: Find the first whole number that makes h > 47 a true statement.

items.q: Hana's paint list. Which rules get a closed circle? Pick all.

options.fb: < has no line under it. 6 is not included, so the circle is open.
> has no line under it. 47 > 47 is false, so the circle is open.

items.fbMiss: One more rule has a line under its symbol. ≤ and ≥ both include the boundary point.
items.fbExtra: One of your picks uses < or >. Those leave the boundary out, so the circle is open.

gates.pass: Hana scrapes off Gus's filled dot and paints an open circle at 47. Gus: "I meant to do that."

gates.title: Gate 2 · Which Way?
gates.prompt: The Mini Drop rule is h < 54 inches. Gus painted the ray to the right. Find which way it should point.
hints: Conceptual: on a number line, numbers get bigger to the right and smaller to the left. The ray covers every number that makes the inequality true.
Procedural: pick a test number on one side of the boundary and put it into the inequality. If it is true, the ray points toward that side.

steps: Test 5 (right of 3): 5 > 3 is true. Test 1 (left of 3): 1 > 3 is false.
The true side is the right, so the ray points right.
worked.q: Which way does the ray point for y ≤ 20?

items.q: Mini Drop rule: h < 54. Which way does the ray point?

options.fb: Right shows heights greater than 54. Test 60: 60 < 54 is false. That rider is too tall for the Mini Drop.
Both ways would make every height a solution. Only heights less than 54 make a true statement.

items.q: Mini Drop rule: h < 54. Which kids can ride? Pick all.

options.fb: 54 < 54 is false. The boundary point is not included in h < 54.
58 < 54 is false. 58 is right of 54, on the wrong side.

items.fbMiss: Another height is less than 54. Decimals can be solutions too.
items.fbExtra: One of your picks makes a false statement. Put it into h < 54 and check.

gates.pass: Gus flips the sign over and paints the ray pointing left. "Left is the good side. For little kids."

gates.title: Gate 3 · Paint It Right
gates.prompt: Graph each rule. Tap the boundary point, pick open or closed, and pick the ray's direction.
hints: Conceptual: the graph has three parts — the boundary point, the circle, and the ray. Each part comes from the inequality.
Procedural: find the number in the rule. Line under the symbol? Closed. No line? Open. Greater points right, less points left.

steps: Practice rule: p ≤ 4. The boundary point is 4.
≤ has a line under it, so 4 is included: closed circle.
≤ means less than or equal, so the ray points left.
worked.q: Graph m > 30: which circle and which direction?

items.q: The Screamer coaster: riders must be at least 48 inches. Graph h ≥ 48.

fb.msg: 50 is a solution, but the graph starts at the boundary point, 48.
46 is too short to ride. The boundary point is the number in the rule, 48.

items.fbDefault: Find 48, the boundary point, and tap it first.
items.fbOpen: The boundary is not included here, so leave the circle open.
items.fbClosed: ≥ includes 48. A rider who is exactly 48 inches can ride, so fill the circle.
items.fbDir: ≥ means 48 or MORE. Taller heights are to the right.

items.q: Kiddie Cups: riders must be younger than 6. Graph a < 6 years.

fb.msg: 5 is a solution, but the circle goes on the boundary point, 6.
7 is too old for the Kiddie Cups. The boundary point is 6.

items.fbDefault: Find 6, the boundary point, and tap it first.
items.fbOpen: < does not include 6. A kid who is exactly 6 is too old, so leave the circle open.
items.fbClosed: This boundary is included, so fill the circle.
items.fbDir: < means younger than 6. Smaller numbers are to the left.

gates.pass: Two clean signs: a closed circle at 48 with a ray to the right, and an open circle at 6 with a ray to the left. Odalys writes it down.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Krank's Inspection
gates.prompt: Mr. Krank checks three signs. Graph the water slide rule, read an old sign, and pick the riders a sign allows.
hints: Conceptual: words have symbols. "At least" is ≥, "no more than" is ≤, "more than" is >, "less than" is <.
Procedural: closed circle means ≤ or ≥, open means < or >. A ray to the right means greater, to the left means less.

steps: Practice sign: a closed circle at 7 with a ray to the left.
Closed means 7 is included: ≤ or ≥. Left means less.
worked.q: A sign shows an open circle at 3 and a ray to the left. What is the rule?

items.q: Water slide: riders weigh no more than 250 pounds. Graph w ≤ 250.

fb.msg: 240 is a solution, but the graph starts at the boundary point, 250.
260 is more than the limit. The boundary point is 250.

items.fbDefault: The boundary point is the number in the rule, 250.
items.fbOpen: The boundary is not included here, so leave the circle open.
items.fbClosed: "No more than 250" lets a rider weigh exactly 250. ≤ includes 250, so fill the circle.
items.fbDir: "No more than" means 250 or LESS. Smaller weights are to the left.

items.q: Gus found an old sign: an open circle at 10 and a ray to the right. Which rule is it?

options.fb: ≥ would need a closed circle. This circle is open, so 10 is not included.
< points left. This ray points right, toward bigger numbers.
That flips both parts. ≤ needs a closed circle and a ray to the left.

items.q: The Spinner sign has a filled-in dot at 42 and a ray to the right. Which heights can ride? Pick all.

options.fb: 41 is left of 42. The ray points right, so 41 is not on the graph.
40.5 is less than 42, so it is not on the ray.

items.fbMiss: Check the boundary point. A closed circle means 42 itself is a solution.
items.fbExtra: One pick is left of 42. The ray only covers 42 and bigger.

gates.pass: Mr. Krank stamps every sign. "Acceptable." From Mr. Krank, that is a party.

journal.heading: Lesson 8-5 — what the sign shop taught us
rows: The number in the rule is where the solution set starts. For h ≥ 48 it is 48. Every graph puts a circle there.
< and > leave the boundary out: open circle (○). ≤ and ≥ include it: closed circle (●). Test it: 47 > 47 is false, so h > 47 gets an open circle.
Numbers get bigger to the right. Greater than points right, less than points left. a < 6 points left.
An open circle at 10 with a ray right is x > 10. A closed circle at 42 with a ray right includes 42 and every height above it.
journal.quote: "Line under the symbol? Fill the circle. No line? Leave a hole for the raccoon." — Bandit

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 8-5 (Understand Inequalities and Their Solutions) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: the boundary point, open versus closed circles, the direction of the ray, and reading a graph back as an inequality.
standards: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint; recognize that such inequalities have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions on number line diagrams
